Tensor index types, indices and symmetries

Source: R/tensor-tensor.R
tensor-indices.Rd

Ports of SymPy's TensorIndexType, TensorIndex, tensor_indices() and TensorSymmetry. An index type has a name, a dummy name (the head of generated dummy index names such as L_0), a dimension and a metric; L$metric, L$delta and L$epsilon are its metric, Kronecker delta and Levi-Civita tensor heads. A TensorIndex is contravariant (is_up) or covariant; unary minus flips it. TensorSymmetry(base, gens) is a monoterm slot symmetry given by a BSGS; TensorSymmetry.fully_symmetric(n) (antisymmetric for n < 0), TensorSymmetry.direct_product(...), TensorSymmetry.riemann() and TensorSymmetry.no_symmetry(n) build the usual ones.

Usage

TensorIndexType(
  name,
  dummy_name = NULL,
  dim = NULL,
  eps_dim = NULL,
  metric_symmetry = 1,
  metric_name = "metric"
)

TensorIndex(name, tensor_index_type, is_up = TRUE)

tensor_indices(s, typ)

TensorSymmetry(...)

TensorSymmetry.fully_symmetric(rank)

TensorSymmetry.direct_product(...)

TensorSymmetry.riemann()

TensorSymmetry.no_symmetry(rank)

Arguments

name

Name (a string).

dummy_name

Head of dummy index names (default: first letter).

dim

Dimension (default: symbol dim_<dummy_name>).

eps_dim

Dimension of the epsilon tensor (default dim).

metric_symmetry

1 symmetric, -1 antisymmetric, 0 no symmetry, NULL no metric.

metric_name

Name of the metric tensor.

tensor_index_type, typ

A TensorIndexType.

is_up

TRUE for a contravariant index.

s

A string of index names, as in symbols().

...

For TensorSymmetry(): a BSGS list(base, gens) or base and gens; for TensorSymmetry.direct_product(): integers, positive for symmetric and negative for antisymmetric groups of indices.

rank

Number of indices; negative for antisymmetric.

Value

A TensorIndexType, TensorIndex, list of indices or TensorSymmetry.

Examples

L <- TensorIndexType("L", dummy_name = "L")
idx <- tensor_indices("i, j", L)
-idx$j
#> -j 
L$metric
#> metric(L,L) 
TensorSymmetry.fully_symmetric(-2)
#> TensorSymmetry((0,), ((0 1)(2 3),)) 
TensorSymmetry.riemann()
#> TensorSymmetry((0, 2), ((0 1)(4 5), (2 3)(4 5), (5)(0 2)(1 3)))
